subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred context-engine maintenance adopt this disabled-by-default operator timeout and generic queue callback even though timed-out plugin work may continue outside the released lane?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but repository policy sets a high bar for new config and fallback surfaces, and code review cannot choose the permanent timeout default or abandonment contract for third-party context-engine workers.

options.title: Approve the opt-in boundary
options.body: Accept the disabled-by-default setting, synchronous queue hook, and host-side fence while documenting that plugin-internal work may continue after timeout.

options.title: Use host-owned timeout policy
options.body: Replace the new operator knob with an owner-selected host default or an existing compaction safety budget, with explicit upgrade proof for long-running plugins.

options.title: Require cooperative cancellation
options.body: Pause this PR until the context-engine contract can propagate cancellation and prove that timed-out workers release plugin-owned locks and resources.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the disabled-by-default setting, synchronous queue hook, and host-side fence while documenting that plugin-internal work may continue after timeout.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the context-engine maintenance and transcript-rewrite owner boundary and are best positioned to decide its timeout and abandonment semantics.
